'''Joshua Shaevitz''' (born 1977) is an American biophysicist and Professor of Physics at the Lewis-Sigler Institute at [[Princeton University]] in [[Princeton, New Jersey|Princeton, NJ]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Joshua Shaevitz {{!}} Department of Physics|url=https://phy.princeton.edu/people/joshua-shaevitz|access-date=2020-10-15|website=phy.princeton.edu}}</ref> He is known for his work in single-molecule [[biophysics]], bacterial growth and motility, and animal behavior.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Shaevitz Lab @ Princeton {{!}} Experimental Biophysics from Molecules to Cells to Animals|url=https://shaevitzlab.princeton.edu/|access-date=2020-10-15|website=shaevitzlab.princeton.edu}}</ref>

== Education and early career ==
Shaevitz completed his bachelor's degree in physics at [[Columbia University]] in New York in 1999 where he was an [https://urf.columbia.edu/urf/research/rabi I. I. Rabi Scholar]. He received his PhD in 2004 from [[Stanford University]] where he studied the molecular motors [[kinesin]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Block|first1=Steven M.|last2=Asbury|first2=Charles L.|last3=Shaevitz|first3=Joshua W.|last4=Lang|first4=Matthew J.|date=2003-03-04|title=Probing the kinesin reaction cycle with a 2D optical force clamp|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=100|issue=5|pages=2351–2356|doi=10.1073/pnas.0436709100|issn=0027-8424|pmc=151344|pmid=12591957|bibcode=2003PNAS..100.2351B|doi-access=free }}</ref> and [[RNA polymerase II|RNA polymerase]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shaevitz|first1=Joshua W.|last2=Abbondanzieri|first2=Elio A.|last3=Landick|first3=Robert|last4=Block|first4=Steven M.|date=2003-12-11|title=Backtracking by single RNA polymerase molecules observed at near-base-pair resolution|journal=Nature|volume=426|issue=6967|pages=684–687|doi=10.1038/nature02191|issn=1476-4687|pmc=1483218|pmid=14634670|bibcode=2003Natur.426..684S}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Abbondanzieri|first1=Elio A.|last2=Greenleaf|first2=William J.|last3=Shaevitz|first3=Joshua W.|last4=Landick|first4=Robert|last5=Block|first5=Steven M.|date=2005-11-24|title=Direct observation of base-pair stepping by RNA polymerase|journal=Nature|volume=438|issue=7067|pages=460–465|doi=10.1038/nature04268|issn=1476-4687|pmc=1356566|pmid=16284617|bibcode=2005Natur.438..460A}}</ref> using [[optical tweezers]] in the group of [[Steven Block]]. Shaevitz then moved to the [[University of California, Berkeley]] as a [[Miller Research Fellows|Miller Fellow]]. There, he focused on the motility of bacteria, including the actin-propelled ''[[Rickettsia rickettsii]]'',<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shaevitz|first1=Joshua W.|last2=Fletcher|first2=Daniel A.|date=2007-10-02|title=Load fluctuations drive actin network growth|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=104|issue=40|pages=15688–15692|doi=10.1073/pnas.0702601104|issn=0027-8424|pmc=2000411|pmid=17895390|arxiv=0708.1791|bibcode=2007PNAS..10415688S|doi-access=free }}</ref> ''[[Myxococcus xanthus]],''<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Mignot|first1=Tâm|last2=Shaevitz|first2=Joshua W.|last3=Hartzell|first3=Patricia L.|last4=Zusman|first4=David R.|date=2007-02-09|title=Evidence that focal adhesion complexes power bacterial gliding motility|journal=Science|volume=315|issue=5813|pages=853–856|doi=10.1126/science.1137223|issn=1095-9203|pmc=4095873|pmid=17289998|bibcode=2007Sci...315..853M}}</ref> and the wall-less [[Spiroplasma]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shaevitz|first1=Joshua W.|last2=Lee|first2=Joanna Y.|last3=Fletcher|first3=Daniel A.|date=2005-09-23|title=Spiroplasma swim by a processive change in body helicity|journal=Cell|volume=122|issue=6|pages=941–945|doi=10.1016/j.cell.2005.07.004|issn=0092-8674|pmid=16179261|s2cid=5070808|doi-access=free}}</ref> Since 2007, Shaevitz has been on the faculty of [[Princeton University]] with appointments in the [https://phy.princeton.edu Department of Physics] and the [http://lsi.princeton.edu Lewis-Sigler Institute for Integrative Genomics] where he holds the rank of Professor.

== Research ==
Shaevitz's work focuses on precision measurements in a variety of biological systems, focusing on topics related to cell shape in bacteria, active matter and pattern formation in groups of moving cells, and the quantification of animal behavior.

His group pioneered the use of 3D live-cell imaging to study the shape of bacteria during growth. In a series of papers, Shaevitz and colleagues unraveled how a cell-wall insertion mechanism with helical coordination can produce cells with the correct shape in both rod and helical This work includes measurement of the [[mechanochemistry]] of individual gliding motors inside live bacteria<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Sun|first1=Mingzhai|last2=Wartel|first2=Morgane|last3=Cascales|first3=Eric|last4=Shaevitz|first4=Joshua W.|last5=Mignot|first5=Tâm|date=2011-05-03|title=Motor-driven intracellular transport powers bacterial gliding motility|journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America|volume=108|issue=18|pages=7559–7564|doi=10.1073/pnas.1101101108|issn=1091-6490|pmc=3088616|pmid=21482768|doi-access=free }}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Balagam|first1=Rajesh|last2=Litwin|first2=Douglas B.|last3=Czerwinski|first3=Fabian|last4=Sun|first4=Mingzhai|last5=Kaplan|first5=Heidi B.|last6=Shaevitz|first6=Joshua W.|last7=Igoshin|first7=Oleg A.|date=May 2014|title=Myxococcus xanthus gliding motors are elastically coupled to the substrate as predicted by the focal adhesion model of gliding motility|journal=PLOS Computational Biology|volume=10|issue=5|article-number=e1003619|doi=10.1371/journal.pcbi.1003619|issn=1553-7358|pmc=4014417|pmid=24810164|arxiv=1401.3220|bibcode=2014PLSCB..10E3619B |doi-access=free }}</ref> and the connection between active matter phase transitions and evolutionarily advantageous fruiting body formation.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Thutupalli|first1=Shashi|last2=Sun|first2=Mingzhai|last3=Bunyak|first3=Filiz|last4=Palaniappan|first4=Kannappan|last5=Shaevitz|first5=Joshua W.|date=2015-08-06|title=Directional reversals enable Myxococcus xanthus cells to produce collective one-dimensional streams during fruiting-body formation|journal=Journal of the Royal Society, Interface|volume=12|issue=109|article-number=20150049|doi=10.1098/rsif.2015.0049|issn=1742-5662|pmc=4535398|pmid=26246416}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Liu|first1=Guannan|last2=Patch|first2=Adam|last3=Bahar|first3=Fatmagül|last4=Yllanes|first4=David|last5=Welch|first5=Roy D.|last6=Marchetti|first6=M. A third thread to Shaevitz's research involves the quantification of animal behavior using supervised and unsupervised machine learning algorithms. Shaevitz and Princeton Neuroscience professor [[Mala Murthy]] published an automated system (LEAP) for measuring animal pose from large movie data sets.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Pereira|first1=Talmo D.|last2=Aldarondo|first2=Diego E.|last3=Willmore|first3=Lindsay|last4=Kislin|first4=Mikhail|last5=Wang|first5=Samuel S.-H.|last6=Murthy|first6=Mala|last7=Shaevitz|first7=Joshua W.|date=January 2019|title=Fast animal pose estimation using deep neural networks|journal=Nature Methods|volume=16|issue=1|pages=117–125|doi=10.1038/s41592-018-0234-5|issn=1548-7105|pmc=6899221|pmid=30573820 |bibcode=2019NatCB..16..117P }}</ref> This has recently been extended to multi-animal data in a package called [https://sleap.ai SLEAP].<ref>{{Cite bioRxiv|last1=Pereira|first1=Talmo D.|last2=Tabris|first2=Nathaniel|last3=Li|first3=Junyu|last4=Ravindranath|first4=Shruthi|last5=Papadoyannis|first5=Eleni S.|last6=Wang|first6=Z. == Scientific activities ==

* [[Aspen Center for Physics]], General Member, 2019–present
* Co-director, NSF Physics Frontier Center for the Physics of Biological Function, 2017–present
* [[Physical Review Letters]] Divisional Associate Editor, 2017–2023
* [[Human Frontier Science Program]] Career Development Award Selection Committee, 2017–2019
* [[American Physical Society]] Division of Biological Physics (DBIO) Member at Large, 2013–2016
* [[American Physical Society]] Division of Biological Physics (DBIO) Executive Committee Chair (2024)<ref>{{Cite web |title=Governance - Unit - DBIO |url=https://engage.aps.org/dbio/governance/executive-committee/committee-members?Execute=1 |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=engage.aps.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Executive Committee - Unit - DBIO |url=https://engage.aps.org/dbio/governance/executive-committee/past-officers |access-date=2024-03-21 |website=engage.aps.org}}</ref>
* [[The Pew Charitable Trusts|Pew Scholars]] Alumni Nomination Review Panel, 2013–2019
